Here is the part of an international call that nobody prepares for. Everyone rehearses the presentation, the numbers, the proposal. Almost nobody rehearses the first ninety seconds, and the first ninety seconds are where the relationship is decided. In those ninety seconds you are asked two questions, always the same two. What does your company do, and what are you working on at the moment. They sound like the same question and they are not. The first one is about the business in general, and the answer never changes. The second one is about this week, and the answer changes every time you speak. People who work well with clients abroad have a clean answer to both, and they can give it in twenty seconds without any notes. That is not fluency. That is preparation, and anybody can do it.

A quick note on what surprised me most about working with a client in England. It was not the accent and it was not the vocabulary. It was the pace of the conversation. In Brazil we start with the business and the friendly part comes later, if there is time. With this client it is the opposite. The first five minutes are about the weather, the weekend, a piece of news that everybody has read. And if you skip that part and go straight to the numbers, the call feels cold to them, even when the numbers are good. So now I keep two or three things ready before every call. Something I read that morning, something about my own week, and one honest question for them. It takes no extra work and it changes the whole tone of the call.
